<tr id="S6.T4.5.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T4.5.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><math id="S6.T4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}=0.5</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.T4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18.2_{\pm 0.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>18.2</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18.2_{\pm 0.2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.T4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".098_{\pm.03}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.098</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.03</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.098_{\pm.03}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">0%</td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">0.46</td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T4.5.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T4.5.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><math id="S6.T4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}=0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}=0.8</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S6.T4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18.3_{\pm 0.3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>18.3</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18.3_{\pm 0.3}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S6.T4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".142_{\pm.04}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.142</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.04</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.142_{\pm.04}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">10%</td>
<td id="S6.T4.5.6.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb">0.71</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We also ablate the overlap threshold <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Very strict thresholds (<math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>) force subspaces to be nearly orthogonal, which achieves excellent load balance (CV .052) but slightly hurts PPL (18.4) because the routing is too rigid. Very loose thresholds (<math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}=0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}=0.8</annotation></semantics></math>) provide insufficient regularization. The value <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}=0.3</annotation></semantics></math> provides the best tradeoff.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate routing rank <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}\in\{16,32,48,64,96\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>96</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}\in\{16,32,48,64,96\}</annotation></semantics></math> on the 350M model. The value <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}=48" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}=48</annotation></semantics></math> gives the best PPL; smaller values underfit because expert subspaces are too constrained, while larger values overfit because subspaces overlap too much, reducing routing discrimination. On the 1.3B model with <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}=64</annotation></semantics></math> is optimal, suggesting a rough heuristic of <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}\approx d/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}\approx d/N</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T5" class="ltx_table">

<div id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 6.4.3 Further Ablations ‣ 6.4 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows the full routing rank ablation. The 0% collapse rate across all <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> values confirms that the Bingham gating mechanism combined with subspace regularization provides robust collapse resistance regardless of the routing rank. The PPL optimum at <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}=48\approx d/N=96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>96</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}=48\approx d/N=96</annotation></semantics></math> is lower than the naive <math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d/N</annotation></semantics></math> estimate, suggesting that some redundancy in the representation space is beneficial for routing discrimination.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">GrMoE’s routing computation (subspace projection followed by Bingham gating) takes 1.3<math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> the time of standard softmax gating. Since routing accounts for fewer than 5% of total MoE forward time, the end-to-end overhead is below 2% (Table <a href="#S6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 6.4.3 Further Ablations ‣ 6.4 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>). The amortization MLP adds another 0.5%.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To put this overhead in context, the dominant cost in an MoE forward pass is the expert FFN computation, which accounts for 85–90% of the total time. The routing computation (whether softmax or GrMoE) accounts for 3–5%, and the remaining 5–10% is attention and embedding. A 1.3<math id="S6.SS4.SSS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> increase in the 3–5% routing component translates to a 1–2% increase in total forward time, which is negligible compared to the benefits in stability and sparsity control.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S6.SS4.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.4.4 </span>Bingham Normalizer Validation</h4>

<div id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We validate the saddle-point approximation to <math id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z(\Lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z(\Lambda)</annotation></semantics></math> by comparing against Monte Carlo estimates (<math id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> samples) at the learned <math id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> values from the 350M and 1.3B models. The learned <math id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> values range from 0.4 to 4.2 across experts and layers. The relative error of the saddle-point approximation is below 1.5% for all encountered values, and the gradient error is below 0.3%. At extreme values (<math id="S6.SS4.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa&gt;10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa&gt;10</annotation></semantics></math>, not encountered during training), the error grows to 5%, but this regime is never reached in practice because the subspace regularization prevents excessive concentration.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">6.4.5 </span>Expert Parallelism Considerations</h4>

<div id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GrMoE’s routing requires all expert frames <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{U_{e}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{U_{e}\}</annotation></semantics></math> to be available on every device for the affinity computation. At <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=16</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}=64</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math>, each frame set occupies <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16\times 2048\times 64\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2048</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>64</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16\times 2048\times 64\times 4</annotation></semantics></math> bytes <math id="S6.SS4.SSS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≈</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx</annotation></semantics></math> 8.4 MB in float32, which is trivially replicable across GPUs. The expert FFN parameters (which dominate memory) are sharded across devices as in standard expert parallelism. The routing computation itself is embarrassingly parallel across tokens and adds negligible communication overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our work connects to three lines of research: MoE routing, geometric methods in deep learning, and load balancing.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Top-<math id="S7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> gating <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer et al., 2017</a>)</cite> and its variants, including Switch <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fedus et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and GShard <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lepikhin et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, remain the dominant routing paradigm. Expert Choice <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2022</a>)</cite> reverses the selection direction for better balance, while StableMoE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2022</a>)</cite> addresses instability via routing consistency regularization. BASE Layers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al., 2021</a>)</cite> simplify MoE training through balanced assignment, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang and others (2024)</a></cite> show that harder tasks benefit from activating more experts, motivating dynamic sparsity control. Soft MoE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Puigcerver et al., 2024</a>)</cite> replaces discrete token-to-expert assignment with soft token mixing, achieving strong perplexity but not fully resolving collapse as our experiments show. DeepSeekMoE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2024</a>)</cite> segments experts into fine-grained routed and shared groups to improve specialization, while SMEAR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Muqeeth et al., 2023</a>)</cite> merges expert parameters adaptively to reduce computational cost. The Qwen series <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2024</a>)</cite> demonstrates that MoE architectures scale effectively across model families with appropriate routing strategies. Recent work on auxiliary-loss-free load balancing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and others, 2024</a>)</cite> proposes alternative balancing strategies that avoid the hyperparameter sensitivity of standard auxiliary losses, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen and others (2025)</a></cite> explore spectral manifold regularization for stable routing. All of these methods operate in flat Euclidean space. GrMoE is the first to exploit Grassmannian structure for routing, and the first to provide formal sparsity guarantees via concentration parameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Hyperspherical embeddings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, hyperbolic neural networks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ganea et al., 2018</a>)</cite>, and Riemannian optimization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Absil et al., 2008</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bécigneul and Ganea, 2019</a>)</cite> have demonstrated benefits in various settings. Our work is the first to apply manifold geometry specifically to MoE routing, and the theoretical results (Theorems <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Concentration–Entropy Bound). ‣ 4 Theoretical Analysis: Concentration and Sparsity ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>–<a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Collapse Resistance via Subspace Separation). ‣ 4 Theoretical Analysis: Concentration and Sparsity ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) provide a formal framework that has no analogue in prior geometric deep learning work. The closest conceptual predecessor is the use of von Mises-Fisher distributions for classification on the hypersphere, but this operates on rank-1 subspaces (directions) rather than the higher-rank subspaces that GrMoE exploits, and it does not provide the concentration-controlled sparsity mechanism that is central to our approach. Recent work on scaling laws for MoE models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Clark et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Krajewski et al., 2024</a>)</cite> has established that routing quality is a key determinant of scaling efficiency, further motivating principled routing mechanisms like GrMoE.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Auxiliary losses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fedus et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, capacity factors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lepikhin et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and expert parallelism strategies address balance as engineering constraints. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and others (2024)</a></cite> recently proposed auxiliary-loss-free balancing via adaptive bias terms, avoiding the hyperparameter sensitivity of loss-based approaches but still operating without geometric structure. Our subspace overlap regularization (Eq. <a href="#S5.E12" title="In 5.3 Training Objective ‣ 5 Amortized Variational Routing ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>) provides a geometric alternative with formal guarantees (Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Collapse Resistance via Subspace Separation). ‣ 4 Theoretical Analysis: Concentration and Sparsity ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), replacing ad hoc balancing with a principled mechanism rooted in the structure of the representation space. The sampled-pairs approximation makes this scale to large <math id="S7.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> without sacrificing effectiveness. We note that our approach is complementary to expert parallelism strategies: GrMoE determines which experts to activate, while expert parallelism determines where those experts are physically located. The two can be combined without modification.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced Grassmannian MoE, a routing framework that operates on the manifold of subspaces and uses Bingham concentration to provide continuous, principled sparsity control. Our theoretical analysis establishes formal connections between concentration parameters and routing entropy, top-<math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> mass, and collapse resistance. By framing expert assignment as exact Bayesian inference with a capacity-aware prior, we elegantly eliminated the need for complex manifold normalizer approximations, resulting in a highly efficient and theoretically complete routing mechanism. Empirically, GrMoE eliminates expert collapse, improves load balance, and enables post-hoc sparsity tuning, achieving better perplexity with more stable training dynamics at both 350M and 1.3B scale.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The broader implication is that MoE routing benefits from respecting the geometric structure of expert specialization: experts specialize in subspaces, and routers should reason about subspaces rather than relying solely on dot products. The token-level analysis confirms that this geometric view yields interpretable routing behavior, with learned concentration values that correlate with linguistic specialization.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Several directions for future work emerge naturally from our framework. First, the Grassmannian routing mechanism could be combined with expert merging or pruning strategies: since each expert has an explicit subspace representation, one can measure subspace overlap to identify redundant experts and merge them without retraining. Recent work on structured pruning of state-space models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> and Fisher-aligned subspace diagnostics for model compression <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al., 2026a</a>)</cite> suggests that subspace-aware pruning criteria can preserve model quality at high compression ratios, and certificate-guided approaches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Farabi Shihab et al., 2026</a>)</cite> provide formal guarantees on pruning quality. Second, the post-hoc sparsity control via <math id="S8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> could be extended to per-layer <math id="S8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> values, allowing different sparsity levels at different depths of the network, connecting to recent work on adaptive compute allocation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al., 2026b</a>)</cite> that learns to dynamically reduce computation in less informative regions. Our preliminary experiments suggest that early layers benefit from lower sparsity (more experts active) while later layers can tolerate higher sparsity, but a systematic study is left for future work. Third, the entropy-based analysis of routing behavior connects to broader work on differentiable entropy regularization for neural optimization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, suggesting that entropy-aware training objectives could further improve the quality of learned subspace representations. Fourth, the Bingham gating mechanism could be applied to other settings where discrete selection over structured alternatives arises, such as attention head selection or mixture-of-depths architectures.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our largest experiment is 1.3B parameters with 16 experts. Scaling behavior on 7B+ models with 64+ experts remains an important open question, though the sampled-pairs approximation to <math id="Sx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{subspace}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>subspace</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{subspace}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the small memory footprint of expert frames (Section <a href="#S6.SS4.SSS5" title="6.4.5 Expert Parallelism Considerations ‣ 6.4 Analysis and Ablations ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4.5</span></a>) suggest no fundamental barrier. The Bingham normalizing constant <math id="Sx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z(\Lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z(\Lambda)</annotation></semantics></math> requires approximation; we validated the saddle-point approximation at all encountered concentration values and found it accurate, but extreme concentrations may require more sophisticated methods. The routing rank <math id="Sx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> is a new hyperparameter that requires tuning, though the heuristic <math id="Sx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{r}\approx d/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{r}\approx d/N</annotation></semantics></math> works well across our experiments. The amortization network provides modest gains over basic GrMoE (0.2 PPL at 350M, 0.3 PPL at 1.3B); whether this gap widens further at larger scale is an open question. Finally, our experiments use a fixed <math id="Sx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math> during training; jointly optimizing <math id="Sx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> during training (or using a curriculum that increases <math id="Sx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> over time) could potentially improve the quality of the learned subspaces, but we leave this exploration to future work.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Proofs</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Concentration–Entropy Bound). ‣ 4 Theoretical Analysis: Concentration and Sparsity ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let the scaled logit for expert <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> be <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{e}=\alpha\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{e}=\alpha\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{e}^{(\alpha)}=\exp(\ell_{e})/Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{e}^{(\alpha)}=\exp(\ell_{e})/Z</annotation></semantics></math> with normalization <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z=\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z=\sum_{j=1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>. Let the mean logit be <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\ell}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{e=1}^{N}\ell_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\ell}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{e=1}^{N}\ell_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the lower bound, the entropy is <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\alpha,x)=\log Z-\sum_{e=1}^{N}g_{e}^{(\alpha)}\ell_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\alpha,x)=\log Z-\sum_{e=1}^{N}g_{e}^{(\alpha)}\ell_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>. By Jensen’s inequality on the convex exponential function, <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z=\sum_{e=1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{e})\geq N\exp(\bar{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z=\sum_{e=1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{e})\geq N\exp(\bar{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math>, which strictly guarantees <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log Z\geq\log N+\bar{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log Z\geq\log N+\bar{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, since <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{(\alpha)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{(\alpha)}</annotation></semantics></math> defines a valid probability simplex, the expected logit is definitively bounded by the maximum logit: <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{e=1}^{N}g_{e}^{(\alpha)}\ell_{e}\leq\max_{e}\ell_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{e=1}^{N}g_{e}^{(\alpha)}\ell_{e}\leq\max_{e}\ell_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>. Substituting these yields:</span></p>
<table id="A1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle H(\alpha,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle H(\alpha,x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\geq\log N+\bar{\ell}-\max_{e}\ell_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mi>e</mi></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\geq\log N+\bar{\ell}-\max_{e}\ell_{e}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E14"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\log N-(\max_{e}\ell_{e}-\bar{\ell})=\log N-\alpha\Delta_{\kappa}(x)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mi>e</mi></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\log N-(\max_{e}\ell_{e}-\bar{\ell})=\log N-\alpha\Delta_{\kappa}(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the exact global upper bound, we express the routing entropy in terms of its derivative. Let the unscaled logit be <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\kappa}_{e}=\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\kappa}_{e}=\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The derivative of entropy with respect to <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is universally <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}H(\alpha,x)=-\alpha\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(\alpha)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Var</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}H(\alpha,x)=-\alpha\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(\alpha)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Integrating from <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, and noting that <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(0,x)=\log N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(0,x)=\log N</annotation></semantics></math>, we secure:</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\alpha,x)=\log N-\int_{0}^{\alpha}s\cdot\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(s)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]\,ds." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>α</mi></msubsup><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>Var</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\alpha,x)=\log N-\int_{0}^{\alpha}s\cdot\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(s)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]\,ds.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">To strictly lower-bound the variance over the integration path, observe that:</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(e)=1/N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(e)=1/N</annotation></semantics></math> is the uniform distribution.
Because <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{(s)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{(s)}</annotation></semantics></math> can thus be written as a mixture <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{(s)}=cU+(1-c)R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{(s)}=cU+(1-c)R</annotation></semantics></math> with bounded weight <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=e^{-s\delta_{\kappa}(x)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=e^{-s\delta_{\kappa}(x)}</annotation></semantics></math> and some valid residual distribution <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>, the variance of <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math> under <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{(s)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{(s)}</annotation></semantics></math> is lower bounded by the variance of the components: <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(s)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]\geq c\mathrm{Var}_{U}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]=e^{-s\delta_{\kappa}(x)}\Gamma_{\kappa}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Var</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Var</mi><mi>U</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>κ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Var}_{g^{(s)}}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]\geq c\mathrm{Var}_{U}[\tilde{\kappa}_{e}]=e^{-s\delta_{\kappa}(x)}\Gamma_{\kappa}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Substituting this minimum variance directly into the integral resolves:</span></p>

<p id="A1.SS1.p3.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p3.4.1" class="ltx_text">Subtracting this evaluated integral from <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log N</annotation></semantics></math> mathematically seals the exact global upper bound.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Proof of Corollary <a href="#Thmcorollary1" title="Corollary 1 (Top-𝑘 Mass Control). ‣ 4 Theoretical Analysis: Concentration and Sparsity ‣ Grassmannian Mixture-of-Experts:Concentration-Controlled Routing on Subspace Manifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a></h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{e}=\alpha\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{e}=\alpha\kappa_{e}\|P_{e}x\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume the experts are strictly sorted by their concentrated affinity such that <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{(1)}\geq\ell_{(2)}\geq\dots\geq\ell_{(N)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{(1)}\geq\ell_{(2)}\geq\dots\geq\ell_{(N)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The probability mass of the top-<math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> experts is aggregated as <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{k}^{(\alpha)}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}g_{(i)}^{(\alpha)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{k}^{(\alpha)}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}g_{(i)}^{(\alpha)}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the remaining trailing mass is identically <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-G_{k}^{(\alpha)}=\sum_{j=k+1}^{N}g_{(j)}^{(\alpha)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-G_{k}^{(\alpha)}=\sum_{j=k+1}^{N}g_{(j)}^{(\alpha)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Taking the respective ratio gives:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1-G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}{G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}=\frac{\sum_{j=k+1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{(j)})}{\sum_{i=1}^{k}\exp(\ell_{(i)})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1-G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}{G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}=\frac{\sum_{j=k+1}^{N}\exp(\ell_{(j)})}{\sum_{i=1}^{k}\exp(\ell_{(i)})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">Given the continuously sorted sequence, every term in the numerator is rigidly bounded above by <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\exp(\ell_{(k+1)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp(\ell_{(k+1)})</annotation></semantics></math>, and every individual term in the denominator is bounded securely below by <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\exp(\ell_{(k)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\exp(\ell_{(k)})</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus:</span></p>
<table id="A1.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1-G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}{G_{k}^{(\alpha)}}\leq\frac{(N-k)\exp(\ell_{(k+1)})}{k\exp(\ell_{(k)})}\leq(N-k)\exp\!\big(-(\ell_{(k)}-\ell_{(k+1)})\big)=(N-k)\exp\!\big(-\alpha\delta_{k}(x)\big)," stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.370em;"
